instruction: Review the most recent email in Notes, identify and extract the largest image from the attached document, saving it as 'largest_image.png' in your home directory.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts image properties (exists, size, format, width, height) from the target file path using PIL Image library
Metric logic correctly compares all required properties: file existence (0.4), size threshold (0.2), format match (0.2), and dimension thresholds (0.2)
Expected values (min_size=35000, format=PNG, min_width=1000, min_height=600) correctly match the metadata description of the actual largest image (40335 bytes, 1114x623)
Getter properly handles edge case where file doesn't exist by returning appropriate default values

LIMITATION: Evaluator can only verify the output file properties, not the process - it cannot verify that user actually reviewed the email, identified the correct attachment, or that the extracted image is truly the largest one from the document. This is acceptable for OSWorld tasks where only final state is verifiable.
The evaluator would pass even if user extracted any image meeting size/format requirements from any source, not necessarily the largest image from the email attachment
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding additional checks if possible, such as verifying specific image content characteristics that would uniquely identify it as the largest image from the known attachment document
Document in metadata that this evaluator only verifies output file properties, not the correctness of the extraction process or source identification
